lines: Changed while in use, nothing lost
Each person's copy is different, and it stays the company's app
The device has the last word
Every change has a named, accountable signer and a working undo
A function can only touch what it declared

web.subject: web app
web.detail: New version did not appear in the open page (still v1 after 1.5 s). After the reload that brings it: half-typed text lost, saved tasks kept.

checks.name: change appears without a reload
half-typed text survives getting the change
saved tasks survive

web.subject: web app
web.detail: A user script starred 2 tasks on v1. After the company shipped v2 (it renamed one CSS class), it starred 0: the person's change broke silently. The company has no way to say where such changes may go.

checks.name: a person can change their own copy
the change survives a company release
the company declares where changes may go

web.subject: web app
web.detail: The server swapped the script for a hostile one. The browser ran it on the next load and it sent the person's tasks to the server. Nothing on the device checked it.

checks.name: code the server swapped in is refused

web.subject: web app
web.detail: Nothing in the page says who is accountable for the running code. After the company rolled back, the open page kept running v2 (confirmed), and the data v2 rewrote stayed rewritten (confirmed).

checks.name: the running code names its signer
a rollback reaches the open app

web.subject: web app
web.detail: The user script declared nothing, read all of the app's stored data, and sent it off the device. The server received it: yes.

checks.name: added code can't read data it didn't declare
added code can't send personal data off the device

web.subject: web app
web.detail: With the network off the app could not even load, and there is no way to hand it a new version from a file. (A service worker can cache the current version; it can't accept a new one offline.)

checks.name: a change can arrive without a network

web.subject: web app
web.detail: The browser gives a screen and, through its accessibility tree, a screen reader (button "Add" found by role: yes). There is no declared list of actions an AI agent can call; an agent has to guess from the page.

checks.name: screen
read aloud
usable by an agent through declared actions

flow.subject: FLOW today
flow.detail: In Chromium a signed release swapped the running code in 14.5 ms while the person was mid-word. Field reads "Buy milk today", focus kept, tasks kept, scroll kept. One catch found on the way: with a plain renderer that rebuilds the field from stored state, a key pressed during the swap was lost in 4 of 6 runs; the app shell must carry the live text across, and this test's shell now does. That belongs in the host (step A2), not in each app. LLP's own web demo rebuilds fields the same plain way, so it likely loses keys too; that was read in its code, not run.

checks.name: change appears without a reload
text typed before, during and after the swap is all there
focus and caret stay in the field
saved tasks survive
scroll position survives a swap

flow.subject: FLOW today
flow.detail: A function signed by the person's own key is refused (untrusted), and there is no document kind for a personal function yet (wrong_type). What exists: the company can open a second spot, and a company release that changes the main app leaves the function in that spot running untouched (confirmed). The person-signed half is step B.

checks.name: a person's own function installs in a spot the company opened
a company release leaves a function in another spot untouched
the company declares where functions may go

flow.subject: FLOW today
flow.detail: Acting as a hostile server we tried five ways to push code or trust: all refused on the device (untrusted, blob, untrusted, untrusted, stale), and the app kept running. Limit: this promise holds for an installed host. When the checker itself is a web page, whoever serves that page can replace the checker.

checks.name: a release signed by the relay's own key is refused
a genuine release with a swapped layer file is refused
a genuine release with edited contents is refused
a new trust list pushed by the relay is refused
an old genuine release replayed later is refused
the app kept running the last good version throughout
the same refusal happens in a real browser

flow.subject: FLOW today
flow.detail: Each accepted release is recorded on the device with the key that signed it. The company undid a release in the open app in 4 ms with data and typing kept, and a crashing release was reverted on its own. Not built: an undo the person triggers on the device, grants for AI agents, and a human-readable name behind a key.

checks.name: every accepted change is recorded with the key that signed it
the company can undo a release in the running app, data and typing kept
a release that crashes is undone automatically
the person can undo a change themselves on the device
an AI agent's change is tied to a time-limited grant from a person

flow.subject: FLOW today
flow.detail: Access is enforced: a function saw none of the tasks or the secret note it hadn't declared, couldn't overwrite a task, and its undeclared network call was refused. The gap: a function that declares both "read tasks" and "network" installs, and the task text reached the network (confirmed). Data has no "personal" label yet, so the device can't refuse that combination. That is step B.

checks.name: a function can't read data it didn't declare
a function can't write data it doesn't own
a function can't use a capability it didn't declare
a function that would send personal data off the device is refused at install

flow.subject: FLOW today
flow.detail: With the network removed (a connection attempt fails), a new trust list, a release and its code installed from a folder of files and the app rendered. A tampered file and an untrusted release in the folder were refused the same way as online.

checks.name: the child process has no network (a connection attempt fails)
`flow install` applies a keyring change and a release from files alone, then renders
a swapped layer file in the bundle is refused
without the keyring change in the bundle, the release is refused (untrusted)

flow.subject: FLOW today
flow.detail: One unchanged function was shown as a browser page, as terminal text, as a spoken description ("Heading: Tasks. 0 of 1 done. Text field: Add a task…. Button…") and as a list of 2 actions that an agent then used to add a task. It works because the function emits meaningful elements, not pixels. Not done: the element meanings aren't fixed in the spec yet, and these presenters are test code, not part of the host.

checks.name: screen (browser DOM)
terminal text
read aloud
an agent lists the actions and uses one
the meaning of each element is fixed in the spec (names, roles, heading levels)
